title: Method of the development of students' foreign language communication skills based on practice with a chatbot
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether integrating chatbot-based foreign-language practice into a university language course can improve students’ communication skills more effectively than traditional classroom instruction alone. The authors argue that chatbots, as AI-based conversational programs, can provide additional opportunities for structured speaking/writing practice, but only if they are embedded into a pedagogically sequenced method rather than used as an isolated tool.

To test this, the authors developed a seven-stage instructional method that combines regular English classes with weekly out-of-class chatbot interaction, followed by in-class analysis and discussion of the chatbot dialogue transcripts. The method was implemented over one semester with first-year university students majoring in linguistics and teacher education at Tambov State University in Russia. A control group (n=25) received traditional instruction only, while an experimental group (n=25) received the same instruction plus chatbot-based practice aligned to course topics such as communication, healthy diet, travelling, and learning.

The study measured ten foreign-language speech skills before and after the intervention using teacher-administered performance tasks and Student’s t-tests. Results showed statistically significant advantages for the experimental group on seven skills, especially asking for information, responding to requests, expressing opinions, arguing, drawing conclusions, and reformulating ideas. No meaningful gains were found for skills the students already performed at a high level, such as initiating dialogue, greeting, and closing conversations. The authors conclude that chatbot-supported practice can be more effective than traditional interaction alone for developing selected communication micro-skills, particularly when the chatbot activity is tied to course content and followed by reflective analysis.
quality_tier_rationale: The study is a semester-long controlled quasi-experiment with a comparison group and pre/post testing, using statistical tests on matched groups. However, it is not randomized and reports limited methodological detail beyond t-tests, so it falls short of blue-tier rigor.
impact_tier_rationale: The chatbot intervention produced statistically significant improvements on several language-fluency micro-skills, but the study does not report standardized effect sizes and the gains are domain-specific rather than broad. That supports a modest, positive impact rather than a large one.

interventions.use_case: step-by-step foreign language communication practice with a chatbot, followed by classroom analysis of the dialogue transcripts to develop speaking micro-skills

finding.finding_summary: In a semester-long quasi-experiment with first-year university EFL students (n=50; 25 control, 25 experimental), the chatbot group outperformed the traditional instruction group on 7 of 10 controlled foreign-language communication skills at posttest. Significant gains favored the chatbot condition for asking for information (t=2.49), responding to partner requests (t=2.24), expressing thoughts, drawing conclusions, stating opinions, giving arguments, and paraphrasing/clarifying (t=4.11), all at p�a0c�a00.05.
finding.measure: Teacher-rated/written-dialectical foreign language communication skill scores across 10 speaking micro-skills; pre/post comparison using Student's t-test

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that chatbot-based practice likely increased learner motivation and reduced anxiety, but these claims are discussed qualitatively rather than measured with a dedicated scale in this study. Evidence is indirect and inferential, drawn from students' engagement with the chatbot and the authors' discussion of prior literature.
finding.measure: Observed engagement and author interpretation; no dedicated motivation/anxiety scale reported in the study
